gen-righteous-gf-nobile: Righteous bends its letters like thin steel rod, with bowls that swell to fill the line. And Nobile keeps its lowercase close to cap height, with open mouths, so the text feels tidy and contemporary beneath it.
gen-righteous-gf-nokora: Nokora lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase, with an s that never tightens, so each line feels friendly and sturdy. Righteous, by contrast, draws every letter in one pencil-like line and fills its bowls with swagger.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Noto Kufi Arabic keeps a welcoming gap in the c and holds its capitals just above the lowercase, which gives it a modern, tidy look. But Righteous has no brush-style swell anywhere, so shrinking it would waste its bold, rod-bent bowls.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans: Glass-tube lettering, hollow and bold. Yet Noto Sans answers it with lowercase bodies that fill most of the letter height, and Righteous gives the pair its loudest, funniest voice.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Righteous cuts its strokes like ribbon of constant width, with bowls that fill the line and a commanding, playful streak. And Noto Sans Adlam does the quieter work, holding its curve endings well apart so text stays clean.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-adlam-unjoine: Every stroke in Righteous carries the same visual weight, like steel rod bent into bowls that fill the line. And Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined leaves generous space where curves meet stems, so extended text moves along smoothly.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hie: Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs points its terminal tips outward and lifts its x-height close to cap height, which looks modern and level. Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs handles steady text, while Righteous, with strokes as wide at the ends as the middle, makes the loud entrance.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Righteous draws its letters like fine rope laid in shape, with bowls that fill the line and plenty of swagger. Noto Sans Armenian takes over for the quieter reading.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Noto Sans Avestan has a pronounced x-height and curve tips that never touch. Righteous earns its keep big and short, where its steel-rod bowls and unvarying stroke thickness can show off.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Righteous has no thick-and-thin contrast to slow the eye, just bowls that fill the line and rod-bent letters. And Noto Sans Balinese gives that punch room to breathe, with open curves and short ascenders.
